subject: Re: DPA redline — controller/processor definitions, logs & embeddings
messages:

Subject: DPA redline and a few clarifications

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Attached is Acme's redline of the DPA (highlights turned on) — primary items we need clarified before legal can sign:

- Roles & definitions: we need explicit language that clarifies Customer is the Controller and Redwood is Processor; there are a few clauses that read as if Redwood may assert controller rights over derived data.
- Telemetry and logs: retention window, scope (are full prompts stored? hashes only?), and ability for Acme to require deletion on demand.
- Embeddings: we need assurance embeddings derived from Acme data cannot be used to train models or be exposed to third parties; also a definition of whether embeddings are "personal data" under GDPR in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: we'd like a 30-day notice and opportunity to object for new subprocessors that handle Acme telemetry or embeddings.
- Execution: Acme uses DocuSign for execution — confirm you'll accept our envelope or if you require Redwood's standard DocuSign flow.

Can your team propose redline responses inline? If acceptable, we'll route back to procurement and trigger execution.

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_20261029.docx (docx, 52KB)

Best,

Hi Amelia — thanks for the redline and the clear list. We've reviewed internally and propose the following high-level positions so we can converge quickly: 

1) Roles: Redwood confirms Customer (Acme) remains Controller for customer-provided input data and any decisions about people. Redwood will be Processor. We do not seek controller status over customer data. To address your "derived data" concern, we propose a carve: Redwood may create aggregated, anonymized telemetry for platform improvement, but we will never treat customer prompt/response contents as controller-owned material.

2) Telemetry/logs: Operational logs will include request metadata (timestamps, model variant, region), request/response token counts, and a scrubbed copy of requests used for debugging. We can commit to a default retention of 90 days for request-level logs and 12 months for aggregated metrics. We will add customer controls: a flag to opt out of request-content retention and a process to request deletion.

3) Embeddings: By default, embeddings derived from Acme inputs will be treated as customer data. Redwood will not use embeddings to re-train models or expose them to other customers. If Acme enables long-term embedding persistence or sharing features, we'll require an explicit opt-in and documentation of the intended use.

4) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current subprocessors list and commit to 30 days' notice for materially new subprocessors. If a new subprocessors materially increase risk (e.g., access to raw prompts/embeddings), Acme can object in writing.

5) Execution: We accept DocuSign. Either party can send the envelope — we can sign Acme's envelope, or we can prepare our own with the agreed addendum. Please confirm preference.

I've attached a response summary PDF and a short suggested clause for the telemetry/embeddings section that Karthik reviewed. If that looks good, Neha can shepherd the updated DPA to procurement and DocuSign.

Attachment: RI_DPA_RESPONSE_20261030.pdf (pdf, 34KB)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett

Laura / Amelia — quick technical clarification to support the proposed language: 

- What we log: request metadata (client id, model, sequence length, region), token counts, and a transient copy of request/response that is retained only for debugging and redaction. We do not persist full prompt histories by default; hashed prompt digests may be kept for deduping and abuse detection.
- Embeddings lifecycle: embeddings are ephemeral unless a customer enables embedding persistence (e.g., to build a vector DB through Redwood-managed storage). When persisted, embeddings are encrypted at rest per customer keys and access-scoped.

Suggested DPA language snippet (technical):
"Redwood, acting solely as Processor, will process Customer Data only on documented instructions from Customer. Operational telemetry (including anonymized aggregations) may be retained for product improvement; request-level content retention defaults to 90 days and may be reduced or eliminated at Customer's direction. Embeddings derived from Customer Data will not be used to train shared models or made available to other customers without explicit Customer consent; persistent embedding storage requires Customer opt-in and will be subject to the protections and retention schedule set forth in this DPA."

I recommend avoiding any phrase that could be read as Redwood asserting Controller status for aggregated metrics. Saying "processor with rights to aggregate anonymized telemetry" is safest.

—Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
